description: We are FirePulse, a team participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our project focuses on analyzing historical MODIS and VIIRS satellite fire data to identify seasonal patterns and make fire activity easier to understand. We are interested in Earth science, data analysis, research, and technology. We welcome collaborators with skills in Python, data science, GIS, web development, UI/UX design, and scientific communication who are passionate about turning satellite data into meaningful insights
summary: Developed by Team NEX, our project addresses critical resolution discrepancies between NASA’s MODIS (1km) and VIIRS (375m) wildfire satellite datasets across multi-year timelines (2014–2024). We built a centralized web platform that harmonizes, aligns, and compares both archives on a single unified interface, transforming isolated data silos into reliable historical analytics. Beyond macro-level satellite monitoring, our end-to-end ecosystem integrates a heat-shielded hexacopter drone equipped with LWIR thermal lenses and environmental sensors. This autonomous UAV detects pre-ignition drought and localized fire risks in real time, effectively bridging historical satellite intelligence with proactive, on-the-ground wildfire prevention.
details: Developed by Team NEX, our project is an end-to-end wildfire intelligence and early-warning ecosystem that bridges multi-decade satellite analytics with autonomous aerial monitoring. First, it addresses the critical spatial and spectral resolution discrepancies between NASA’s MODIS (1 km) and VIIRS (375 m) wildfire datasets across multi-year timelines (2016–2025). Using a centralized, interactive web platform, the system ingests, calibrates, and harmonizes both satellite archives into a single unified interface, allowing analysts to compare historical fire trends side-by-side without sensor-induced distortion. Second, the platform connects this macro-level historical intelligence with micro-level, real-time intervention by deploying a custom heat-shielded hexacopter drone. Equipped with Long-Wave Infrared (LWIR) thermal imaging and environmental sensors, the autonomous UAV patrols high-risk zones to detect pre-ignition drought conditions and localized thermal anomalies before flames erupt.
